headline: PM Tarique arrives in Dubai en route to Dhaka after UNGA visit
summary: The Prime Minister reached Dubai International Airport yesterday following a five-day visit to New York for the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Dubai International Airport at 8:23pm (Dubai time) yesterday. He was accompanied by his wife, Zubaida Rahman, and other members of his entourage.
The stopover comes after a five-day visit to New York, where the Prime Minister attended the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA).
During the session, he delivered his maiden address to the General Debate, highlighting Bangladesh's positions on global peace, climate change, and the Rohingya crisis.
The Prime Minister also engaged in a packed schedule of bilateral meetings with world leaders, UN officials, development partners, and international organization representatives.
He is scheduled to depart Dubai for Dhaka via Emirates flight EK582 at 2:00am on September 27, with an expected landing at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 8:40am the same day.
caption:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has reached Dubai on his way home from New York.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Dubai International Airport at 8:23pm (Dubai time) yesterday. He was accompanied by his wife, Zubaida Rahman, and other members of his entourage.

During the session, he delivered his maiden address to the General Debate, highlighting Bangladesh's positions on global peace, climate change, and the Rohingya crisis.

The Prime Minister also engaged in a packed schedule of bilateral meetings with world leaders, UN officials, development partners, and international organization representatives.

He is scheduled to depart Dubai for Dhaka via Emirates flight EK582 at 2:00am on September 27, with an expected landing at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 8:40am the same day.

headline: Kane's penalty miss: Spain beats England 3-2 in Nations League opener
summary: The world champions maintained their 39-match unbeaten streak after overcoming a 2-1 deficit at Wembley.
details: World champions Spain secured a 3-2 victory over England in their Nations League opener at Wembley, extending their unbeaten run to 39 matches.
The match began with an early lead for Spain through Lamine Yamal, who capitalized on a defensive error by Marc Guehi in the second minute.
England fought back to take a 2-1 lead within 40 minutes, with goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane, who scored with a diving header.
A critical turning point occurred in the 55th minute when Harry Kane missed a penalty, hitting the crossbar after losing his balance during the shot.
Spain equalized in the 60th minute through Alex Baena, following another defensive mistake by Nico O'Reilly.
The winning goal came in the 74th minute when Mikel Oyarzabal scored with a chip over goalkeeper James Trafford, assisted by Alex Baena.
England coach Thomas Tuchel expressed disappointment as his team failed to capitalize on their lead, while Spain coach Luis de la Fuente celebrated the comeback win.
caption:
A penalty miss and defensive blunders cost England. Spain remains unbeaten in 39 games!

World champions Spain secured a 3-2 victory over England in their Nations League opener at Wembley, extending their unbeaten run to 39 matches.

The match began with an early lead for Spain through Lamine Yamal, who capitalized on a defensive error by Marc Guehi in the second minute.

England fought back to take a 2-1 lead within 40 minutes, with goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane, who scored with a diving header.

A critical turning point occurred in the 55th minute when Harry Kane missed a penalty, hitting the crossbar after losing his balance during the shot.

Spain equalized in the 60th minute through Alex Baena, following another defensive mistake by Nico O'Reilly.

The winning goal came in the 74th minute when Mikel Oyarzabal scored with a chip over goalkeeper James Trafford, assisted by Alex Baena.

England coach Thomas Tuchel expressed disappointment as his team failed to capitalize on their lead, while Spain coach Luis de la Fuente celebrated the comeback win.
